subject: OrbisHealth dedicated reservation structure & ramp workplan
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@orbishealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: OrbisHealth dedicated reservation structure & ramp workplan

Lena — thanks for the call this morning. As promised, I’m sending a concise set of reservation options tied to the throughput estimates you shared (peak inference windows and expected 99th‑percentile latency targets). The goal here is to present 3 pragmatic paths you can choose from depending on risk tolerance and budget: Conservative (fast warm start, higher minimum), Balanced (recommended), and Elastic (lower floor plus burst).

Key assumptions (please confirm):
- Production traffic peaking ~1,200 concurrent requests during 0900–1700 PT.
- Avg token length 120 tokens; tail usage up to 1,000 tokens for inference tasks.
- Target P99 generation latency <= 300ms for small model tier; 500–700ms acceptable for larger retrieval-heavy jobs.

Highlights of the attached workbook: Orbis_Reserve_Options_v3.xlsx
- Option A — Conservative: 48 dedicated A100-equivalent GPUs minimum; 2-stage ramp to 96 over 6 months; priority lane for high-value endpoints; warm cache pre-seeding.
- Option B — Balanced (recommended): 24 dedicated GPUs minimum; ramp to 48 over 4 months with scheduled burst credits; automatic fallback to regional hosted pool for non-critical requests.
- Option C — Elastic: 12 dedicated GPUs minimum; aggressive burst + shared-host fallback; cost-optimized for pilot stages but higher latency variance during sustained peaks.

Proposed ramp cadence (example for Option B):
- Week 0: 24 GPUs live, pre-warm critical models and KV cache for 2 most-used endpoints.
- Week 4: Add 8 GPUs (32 total) — enable 2 additional model variants.
- Week 12: Add 16 GPUs (48 total) — move into full production throughput config.

Commercial notes:
- We can structure credits to offset warmup burn in month 1 (typically 10–15% of committed spend).
- Early-exit clauses at month 3 and month 6 with defined decommit windows if usage materially diverges.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm which Option you prefer (A/B/C).
2) Procurement: agree on invoice cadence and minimal term (we typically do a 6‑month minimum on Balanced/Conservative options).
3) Technical kickoff (30–45 minute) to map model pinning, routing policies, and KV-cache pre-seed lists.

I’ve also included a quick sensitivity tab in the workbook that shows token-cost and P99 latency tradeoffs across GPU mixes. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk through this with Marcus & procurement.

Regards,

Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555‑0142
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OrbisHealth dedicated reservation structure & ramp workplan

Aditya — thanks for the clear options and workbook. A few clarifying items from our side after an internal sync: 

1) For our primary clinical-inferencing endpoint, latency consistency is more important than raw throughput; we lean toward lower tail latency even at a moderate cost premium. That pushes us toward Option B with a bias to Option A for that endpoint only.
2) Procurement sees the 6‑month minimum as acceptable if there’s a mid-term break provision; please provide the exact language for the early-exit and decommit windows so we can share with legal.
3) Can you confirm whether warm-cache pre-seeding will be an operational task for our infra team or if Redwood will handle the pre-seed and verification? If we must do it, we need a runbook and an estimate of time required (FTE hours).

Also looping Lena to weigh in on ramp dates — our launch window is late Q3 (target 2027‑09‑20) for the first tranche of customers. If we proceed with Option B and the proposed ramp cadence, will that timing look feasible?

Thanks,
Marcus Hale
VP, Product — OrbisHealth
marcus.hale@orbishealth.com

Subject: Re: OrbisHealth dedicated reservation structure & ramp workplan

Marcus — thanks for the clear points. Short answers up front, then an updated ask and next-steps.

1) Tail latency preference: Understood. We recommend Option B as baseline but will reserve a 12‑GPU hot lane (subset of the fleet) configured with tighter scheduling and higher pre-warm thresholds dedicated to your clinical endpoint — effectively giving you the latency consistency of Option A for that critical path while keeping overall committed footprint in Balanced.

2) Early-exit language: Draft clause suggested below for your legal team to review (we can put this into a SOW/Annex):
"If average committed utilization is consistently < 40% for a continuous 30‑day window after month 3, either party may trigger a decommit review. Decommitments during the initial 6‑month term require 30‑day notice and are subject to a 10% early termination fee of the remaining committed spend."

3) Cache pre-seeding: Redwood will handle pre‑seed and verification for the initial activation (no additional FTE from Orbis required). We’ll provide a short runbook and a verification checklist. Typical pre-seed time: 1–2 business days of Redwood ops time, plus a 2‑hour coordination window with your infra/security to validate network rules.

I’ve attached a revised workbook with the hot-lane variant and a cost column reflecting the incremental premium for the hot lane. Also attaching a DocuSign stub so procurement can start internal routing.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Orbis confirms Option B + hot lane by EOD Monday (2027‑07‑05) to lock target launch cadence.
- Procurement to confirm invoicing cadence and provide the PO contact for DocuSign.
- Technical kickoff (we suggest July 8 or July 9) — 30 minutes to align on model pinning and KV pre-seed targets.

If that timeline works I’ll ask Monica to kick off the SOW and share a first draft.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
